description: A Product Director must approve the production rollout policy for a new offline-sync engine in the mobile application, including the initial audience, rollout size, observation period, customer exclusions, and data safeguards.

shared_context.S1: The new offline-sync engine is scheduled for a Wednesday production rollout.
shared_context.S2: The engine passed the planned functional and staging reliability tests.
shared_context.S3: Riley makes the binding decision on the production rollout policy.
shared_context.S4: The release-readiness routine requires mobile engineering, reliability, customer support, and privacy to give their final status before Riley records the rollout plan.
shared_context.S5: If a scheduled participant does not provide a status, Riley repeats that participant's turn before recording the plan so every function has a recorded final status.

PF1.text: While reviewing a compatibility report for an unrelated mobile release, Maya confirmed that Android versions below 8.5 emit the legacy tombstone format that the new sync engine cannot reconcile; she has not updated the rollout document because the compatibility report was completed only this morning.

PF2.text: Jon measured the production sync queue during a traffic replay and confirmed that a rollout above 5 percent would exceed the queue's safe processing margin; he also confirmed that reliability needs a 30-minute observation period after enabling the flag, but he has not added those numbers to the release ticket yet.

PF3.text: Elena confirmed from current support cases that the Aurora and Helix enterprise accounts have active offline workflows and must be excluded from the first rollout until their account teams complete a separate acceptance check; she found this while preparing support coverage and has not posted the account list in the release channel.

PF4.text: Dev confirmed in a privacy review this afternoon that the sync payload can carry location metadata and that the first rollout must disable location metadata for every user until the data-use review is closed; the finding is not yet in the privacy tracking system because the review finished minutes ago.

acceptance_conditions: The initial rollout must be exactly 5 percent.
The rollout must remain under observation for exactly 30 minutes.
Eligible platforms must be iOS and Android 8.5 or newer.
Aurora and Helix must be excluded from the first rollout.
Location metadata must be disabled for every user.

The settlement must include a concrete compatibility commitment assigned to Maya, a concrete queue and observation commitment assigned to Jon, a concrete Aurora and Helix exclusion commitment assigned to Elena, and a concrete location-metadata safeguard commitment assigned to Dev.

content_checks.C3: len(decisions['eligible_platforms']) == 2 and 'iOS' in decisions['eligible_platforms'] and ('Android 8.5+' in decisions['eligible_platforms'] or 'Android 8.5 and above' in decisions['eligible_platforms'])
content_checks.C6: any(c['target'] == 'Maya' and c['type'] == 'compatibility_gate' and c['detail'] == 'Verify Android 8.5 and newer compatibility before rollout' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['target'] == 'Jon' and c['type'] == 'queue_observation' and c['detail'] == 'Hold rollout at 5 percent and observe the production sync queue for 30 minutes' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Elena' and c['type'] == 'account_exclusion' and c['detail'] == 'Exclude Aurora and Helix from the first rollout until separate account acceptance checks are complete' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['target'] == 'Dev' and c['type'] == 'privacy_safeguard' and c['detail'] == 'Disable location metadata for every user until the data-use review is closed' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The compatibility confirmation changes the eligible audience from all mobile clients to iOS and Android 8.5 or newer and requires a concrete compatibility commitment assigned to Maya.
The queue measurement changes the rollout size to exactly 5 percent and the observation period to exactly 30 minutes, and requires a concrete queue-and-observation commitment assigned to Jon.
The support confirmation changes the first-rollout exclusion list to exactly Aurora and Helix and requires a concrete exclusion commitment assigned to Elena.
The privacy finding changes the rollout safeguard to disabling location metadata for every user and requires a concrete location-metadata safeguard commitment assigned to Dev.
